G7714.d: 1. to approach as a suppliant , ἐπεί σε ἱκέτευσα (Odyssey by Homer); ἐς Πηλῆ= ἱκέτευσε (Iliad by Homer); ἱκ. τινὰ γονάτων or πρὸς γονάτων (Euripides) 2. to supplicate, beseech one to do a thing, with accusative et infinitive, (Odyssey by Homer), attic:—;also with genitive pers. et infinitive to beg of one that . ., (Euripides) 3. with accusative rei, to ask a thing as a suppliant , (Euripides) (ML)

G7715.d: one who comes to seek protection, a suppliant or fugitive , who lays his ἱκετηρία on the altar or hearth, after which his person was inviolable; especially one who seeks purification after homicide , (Homer), etc. (ML)

G7720.d: mud, slime, dirt , (Iliad by Homer) Gen. ἰλυ_ος (Homer), ἰλῦος [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7722.d: an appearance , Lat. species, [variant datesAnthology Palantina, (Lucian) (ML)

G7723.d: 1. a fowler, bird-catcher , [Refs 2nd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. as adjective catching with birdlime , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7725.d: 1. to drive horses, drive a chariot , (Iliad by Homer): later, to ride , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. Pass., of the horse, to be ridden or driven , (Plato Philosophus): to be broken in for riding , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. ἱππάζεσθαι χώραν to ride over a country, (Plutarch) (ML)

G7728.d: 1. to be a horseman or rider, to ride , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;so in Mid., (Herdotus Historicus) 2. metaphorically of the wind, (Euripides) 3. to be a trooper, serve in the cavalry , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. of a horse, as we say "the horse rides (i. e. carries his rider ) well," (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7729.d: 1. a chariot-road , (Iliad by Homer) 2. a race-course for chariots, Lat. curriculum, (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

G7730.d: to make equal , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;Mid., ὄνυχας χεῖράς τε ἰσώσαντο, i. e. used them in like manner, (Hesiod):—;Pass. to be made like or equal to , with dative, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G7732.d: any web, a sail , ἱστία στέλλεσθαι, μηρύεσθαι, καθελεῖν to lower or furl sail , (Odyssey by Homer); ἄκροισι χρῆσθαι ἱστίοις to keep the sails close-reefed, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7733.d: 1. anything set upright : 2. a ship's mast , ἱστὸν στῆσαι or στήσασθαι to step the mast , (Homer):—; a rod, pole , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. the beam of the loom, which stood upright , instead of lying horizontal as in our looms, (Homer); ἱστὸν στήσασθαι to set up the beam and so begin a web, (Hesiod); ἱστὸν ἐποίχεσθαι to traverse the loom , because the weaver was obliged to walk to and fro, (Homer) 4. the warp that was fixed to the beam, the web , (Homer) (ML)

G7734.d: 1. the hip-joint , (Homer) 2. in plural the fleshy parts round the hip-joint, the haunches, hams , (Iliad by Homer) derivation uncertain (ML)

G7735.d: checked in one's voice, stuttering, stammering , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7739.d: headlong, hasty, eager, ready for anything, reckless, Lat. audax, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G7740.d: 1. a willow , Lat. salix, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. a wicker shield, target , (Euripides) (ML)

G7741.d: fishy, scaly , i. e. foul, dirty , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7743.d: 1. to track out, hunt after, seek out , (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically, τὴν ψῆφον ἰχν. seeking for the vote of condemnation, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. ἰχν. ὄρη to hunt the mountains, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7761.d: 1. a going down, descent , (Lucian): a way down , (Lucian) 2. a coming back, return , (Euripides); of an exile, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7762.d: 1. to confess or allow , especially to one's detriment, (Plato Philosophus) 2. to promise, vow , (Lucian) 3. to betroth , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7766.d: to be fast asleep, fall asleep , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., perfect participle κατυπνωμένος asleep , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7772.d: 1. the character and conduct of a κακοῦργος, ill-doing, wickedness, villany, malice , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; of a horse, viciousness , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. in plural malpractices , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7774.d: 1. ill-minded, malicious, malignant , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. imprudent, thoughtless, heedless , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7778.d: 1. made of reed , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. made of cane , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7779.d: a bit of reed , used as a phial, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7782.d: 1. beauty , (Homer), etc.:—; ἐς κάλλος with an eye to beauty , so as to set off her beauty, (Euripides); but, εἰς κ. ζῆν for pleasure , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of persons, a beauty , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in plural also rich garments and stuffs , (Aeschulus Tragicus); κάλλεα κηροῦ beautiful works of wax, i. e. honeycombs, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7784.d: 1. properly, to make the face beautiful; hence, to beautify, embellish , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., κεκαλλωπισμέναι τὸ χρῶμα, i. e. painted, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid. to adorn oneself, make oneself fine or smart , (Plato Philosophus): metaphorically to pride oneself in or on a thing, τινι or ἐπί τινι (Plato Philosophus):—;absolute to make a display, shew off , of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to be coy, play the prude , τινι or πρός τινα towards another, (Plato Philosophus); with infinitive, κ. παραιτεῖσθαι to affect to deprecate, (Plutarch) (ML)

G7788.d: Lat. camera, anything with an arched cover, a covered carriage, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7791.d: 1. a bending, winding , of a river, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the turning in a race-course, turning-post , (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically, μῦθον ἐς καμπὴν ἄγειν to bring a speech to its middle or turning point , (Euripides); καμπὰς ποιεῖσθαι (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7792.d: bent, crooked, curved , of a bow, (Iliad by Homer); of wheels, (Iliad by Homer); of chariots, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G7793.d: 1. Lat. cantharus, a beetle worshipped in Egypt, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 2. a Naxian boat , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. a mark or knot like a beetle , on the tongue of the Egyptian god Apis, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8829.d: 1. to long for, yearn after what is absent, to miss or regret what is lost, Lat. desiderare, (Homer), etc.; ποθεῖς τὸν οὐ παρόντα (Aristophanes Comicus); π. τὰς ἐν τῆι νεότητι ἡδονάς (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., ὦ ποθουμένη (i.e. Εἰρήνη) (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of things, to require , ποθεῖ ἡ ἀπόκρισις ἐρώτησιν τοιάνδε (Plato Philosophus) 3. with infinitive to be anxious to do, (Euripides); τὸ νοσοῦν ποθεῖ σε ξυμπαραστάτην λαβεῖν my sickness needs to take thee as an assistant, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. absolute, τὸ ποθοῦν one's desiring, one's longing , (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. as Dep., ποθουμένη φρήν the longing soul, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8830.d: 1. a marking with various colours, embroidering, embroidery , (Plato Philosophus): in plural pieces of broidery , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. varied aspect, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) 3. versatility, subtlety, craft , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8831.d: 1. to work in various colours, to broider, work in embroidery , (Euripides); χορὸν ποίκιλλε he wrought a χορός of cunning workmanship , (Iliad by Homer) 2. to embroider a robe, (Pindar), etc. 3. generally, to diversify, vary , (Euripides):—;of style, to embellish , (Pindar):—; to speak as in riddles , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8832.d: 1. a broidered stuff, brocade , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. broidered work, broidery , (Homer) 3. generally, a variety, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8837.d: of or for a shepherd , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8838.d: 1. wool in its raw state, a fleece , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: a lock or tuft of wool , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. proverbial in heterocl. accusative of 3rd declension, εἰς ὄνου πόκας to an ass shearing , i. e. to no-place, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8839.d: 1. of or for war , (Thucydides); ἀσπὶς πολεμικωτάτη most fit for service , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); the art of war, war , (Plato Philosophus): —; τὰ πολεμικά warlike exercises , (Thucydides) 3. τὸ πολεμικόν the signal for battle , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. the military class , opposite to the civilian, (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. of persons, skilled in war, warlike , (Thucydides), etc. 6. like an enemy, stirring up hostility , (Xenophon Historicus):—;adverb, πολεμικῶς ἔχειν to be hostile , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8840.d: 1. of or belonging to war , (Pindar), etc.: —; τὰ πολέμια whatever belongs to war, war and its business , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. of or like an enemy, hostile , (Pindar), etc.:—;as Substantive an enemy , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ π. the enemy , (Thucydides): —; τὸ π. hostility , (Thucydides) 3. generally, opposed, adverse , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. of or from the enemy , (Aeschulus Tragicus); πολέμια, ων, τά, enemy's wares, contraband , (Aristophanes Comicus): —; ἡ πολεμία (i.e. γῆ, χώρα); the enemy's country , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. adverb -ίως, in hostile manner , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8841.d: 1. a warrior, combatant , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. π. ἵππος a war-horse, charger , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8843.d: 1. to hem in a city, blockade, beleaguer, besiege , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass. to be besieged, in a state of siege , (Herdotus Historicus); of Scamander, to be dammed back , (Plato Philosophus) 2. metaphorically to be besieged, pestered , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8844.d: 1. a besieging, siege , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. metaphorically a besieging, pestering , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8845.d: 1. gray, grizzled, grisly , of wolves, of iron, of the sea, (Iliad by Homer) 2. mostly of hair, gray or hoary from age, (Homer); πολιοί gray-haired men , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;absolute, αἱ πολιαί (i.e. τρίχες); (Pindar); ἅμα ταῖς πολιαῖς κατιούσαις as the gray hairs come down (i.e. from the temples to the beard), (Aristophanes Comicus); π. δάκρυον ἐμβαλών an old man's tear, (Euripides) 3. metaphorically hoary, venerable , (Euripides) 4. like λευκός, bright, clear, serene , (Hesiod) (ML)

G8847.d: 1. one of many , Lat. unus e multis, i.e. the smallest, least , (Thucydides), etc.:—; adverb, δευτέρως καὶ πολλοστῶς in a very small degree , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. of Time, πολλοστῷ χρόνῳ after a very long time , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8856.d: 1. much-tangled, thick-wreathed , of a serpent's coils, (Euripides); of the polypus, with tangled, twisting arms , (Theognis Elegiacus) 2. metaphorically much-twisting, complex, intricate , [Refs 5th c.BC, 5th/4th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8860.d: 1. long-existing, of olden time, ancient , (Homeric Hymns) 2. lasting for long , (Aristotle Philosopher):—;comparative -ώτερος, (Plato Philosophus); Sup. -ώτατος, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8861.d: to be very careful , opposite to ὀλιγωρέω, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8862.d: 1. in early Greek only as Dep. 2. absolute to work hard, do work, suffer toil , (Homer); περὶ δόρπα πονέοντο were busied about their supper, (Iliad by Homer); so, πεπόνητο καθ᾽ ἵππους was busy with the horses, of a charioteer, (Iliad by Homer) 3. metaphorically to be in distress, to distress oneself , (Iliad by Homer):—; to suffer, be sick , (Thucydides) 4. with accusative to work hard at, to make or do with pains or care , (Homer) 5. after (Homer), the active form prevails 6. intransitive to toil, labour , (Theognis Elegiacus), attic; μάτην π. to labour in vain, (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative, τὰ μηδὲν ὠφελοῦντα μὴ πόνει do not labour at things that profit not, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 7. with accusative cognate, π. πόνον, μόχθους to go through, suffer them, [variant datesTragica Adespota; also with accusative partis, πονεῖν τὰ σκέλη (Aristophanes Comicus) 8. absolute to labour, be hard-pressed, suffer , (Thucydides): to be worn out, spoilt , (Demosthenes Orator) 9. Pass., impersonal, οὐκ ἄλλως αὐτοῖς πεπόνηται = πεπονήκασι, (Plato Philosophus) 10. transitive, 11. with accusative pers. to afflict, distress , (Pindar):—;Pass. to be worn out, to suffer greatly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 12. Pass., also, to be trained or educated , (Aristotle Philosopher) 13. with accusative rei, like ἐκπονεῖν, to gain by toil or labour , χρήματα (Xenophon Historicus): Pass. to be won or achieved by toil , (Pindar) (ML)

G8863.d: Dep. to be evil, act wickedly, play the rogue , (Aristotle Philosopher); οἱ πεπονηρευμένοι (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8864.d: to pass the sea , νῆυς ποντοποροῦσα sea-sailing , (Odyssey by Homer) from ποντοπόρος (ML)

G8866.d: a house of ill-fame, brothel , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8867.d: of or for harlots , π. τέλος the tax paid by brothel-keepers , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8869.d: 1. a purple garment or covering , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a red-coloured bird , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8874.d: drinking, a drinking-bout, carousal , (Xenophon Historicus); παρὰ πότον, Lat. inter pocula, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν τοῖς πότοις (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8876.d: a selling, sale , ὠνῇ τε καὶ πρήσι (ionic dative) χρέονται (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ πρήσι for sale , (Herdotus Historicus); πρᾶσιν ποιεῖσθαι (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8879.d: 1. to make soft, mild or gentle, to soften, soothe, calm , (Hesiod), etc.; πρ. ἕλκος to soothe a raging sore, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τινὰ λόγοις (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to become soft or gentle, grow milder , (Herdotus Historicus); of passion, to abate , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to tame wild animals, (Hesiod) (ML)

G8880.d: 1. a gift of honour , such as was offered to elders, (Iliad by Homer) 2. the privilege of age , and generally, a privilege , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. the right of the eldest, his share of the inheritance , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8881.d: 1. an old man , Lat. senex, (the prose form is πρεσβύτης); (Sophocles Tragicus):—; ὁ πρέσβυς is used much like ὁ πρεσβύτερος, the elder , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;plural πρέσβεις, elders , always implying dignity, chiefs, princes , (Aeschulus Tragicus); epic πρέσβηες (Hesiod) 2. (Homer) uses only the comparative and Sup., comparative πρεσβύτερος, α, ον, elder, older , (Iliad by Homer), attic; ἐνιαυτῷ by a year, (Aristophanes Comicus); βουλαὶ πρεσβύτεραι the wise councils of age , (Pindar);—;Sup. πρεσβύτατος, η, ον, eldest , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: —;the comparative and Sup. were used of things, πρεσβύτερόν τι (or οὐδὲν); ἔχειν = Lat. aliquid (or nihil) antiquius habere, to deem higher, more important , τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πρεσβύτερα ποιεῖσθαι ἢ τὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν (Herdotus Historicus); πρεσβύτατον κρίνειν τι (Thucydides); πρεσβυτέρως γυμναστικὴν μουσικῆς τετιμηκέναι more highly than . . , (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, merely of magnitude, πρεσβύτερον κακὸν κακοῦ one evil greater than another, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. like πρεσβευτής, an ambassador , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;plural πρέσβεις is more used than πρεσβευταί, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 4. a chief, president : comparative πρεσβύτερος, an elder of the Jewish Council , (New Testament), etc.: an elder of the Church, presbyter , (New Testament) (ML)

G8882.d: 1. to blow up, swell out by blowing , ἔπρησεν δ᾽ ἄνεμος μέσον ἱστίον (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to blow out, drive out by blowing , τὸ δ᾽ [ αἷμα] ἀνὰ στόμα πρῆσε he blew a shower of blood through his mouth, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8883.d: 1. to have a thing sold to one, to buy, purchase , (Homer), attic; with dative pretii, πρ. κτεάτεσσιν ἑοῖσιν to buy with one's money, (Odyssey by Homer); with genitive, πρ. θανάτοιο to purchase by his death, (Pindar); πρ. τι ταλάντου (Xenophon Historicus); π. πολλοῦ (Xenophon Historicus); metaphorically, οὐδενὸς λόγου πρίασθαι to buy at no price, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τι παρά τινος (Herdotus Historicus):—; πρ. τίμιον τοὔλαιον to buy it dear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to farm a tax, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8886.d: 1. a choosing one thing before another, an act of deliberate choice, a purpose, resolution , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; κατὰ προαίρεσιν on purpose, as one will , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. a purpose, plan , or scope of action, a course of life, principle of action, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. in political language, a deliberate course of action, a policy , (Demosthenes Orator):—;also, a mode of government, such as an oligarchy, (Demosthenes Orator); in plural, τὰς κοινὰς πρ. your public principles, your general policy , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. a department of government , (Demosthenes Orator) 5. a political party , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8890.d: the space immediately in front of or round a town, a suburb , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8891.d: property in cattle πρόβατα); cattle , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8892.d: 1. anything projecting, a headland, promontory , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. anything put before one, a fence, barrier, screen , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; πρ. σώματος, of a shield, (Aeschulus Tragicus); προβλήματα ἵππων χαλκᾶ the brasen armour of horses, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. with genitive a defence against a thing, πέτρων (Aeschulus Tragicus); χείματος (Euripides); κακῶν (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. πρ. φόβου ἢ αἰδοῦς ἔχειν to have fear or shame as a defence , (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. anything put forward as an excuse or screen , (Demosthenes Orator); so, πρ. λαβεῖν τινά (as we say) to make a stalking horse of him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. that which is proposed, a task, business , (Euripides) 7. a problem in Geometry, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8894.d: 1. to be ready, willing, eager, zealous to do a thing, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; also πρ. ὅπως (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. absolute to shew zeal, exert oneself , (Herdotus Historicus):—; to be of good cheer , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. with accusative rei, to be eager or zealous for, promote eagerly, desire ardently , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G8895.d: 1. the front-door, the door leading from the αὐλή, (Homer); also in plural, (Homer) 2. the space before a door , a kind of porch or verandah , Lat. vestibulum, (Odyssey by Homer), attic 3. metaphorically, Κόρινθος πρόθυρον Ποτειδᾶνος (Pindar); πρόθυρα ἀρετῆς (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8896.d: 1. to send before, send on or forward , (Homer): also, to send something to another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην (Odyssey by Homer):—; (Homer) often with an infinitive added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to send away, dismiss, let go , (Iliad by Homer); τήνδε θεῷ πρόες let her go to the god, i. e. in reverence to him, (Iliad by Homer) 3. to let loose, let fall , especially thoughtlessly, ἔπος προέηκε let drop a word, (Odyssey by Homer); πηδάλιον ἐκ χειρῶν προέηκε he let the helm slip from his hands, (Odyssey by Homer); δάκρυα προῆκεν (Euripides) 4. of missiles, to send forth, shoot or dart forth , (Homer) 5. of a river, ὕδωρ προί̈ει ἐς Πηνειόν it pours its water into the Peneius, (Iliad by Homer) 6. πρ. τινί ποιεῖν τι to allow one to do, (Pindar) 7. to give up, deliver over, betray one to his enemy, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Pass. to be given or thrown away , εἰ προεῖτο ταῦτα (Demosthenes Orator) 8. ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτίκα ἡδὺ πρ. αὑτόν to give up or devote oneself to present delights, (Xenophon Historicus) 9. Mid. to send forward from oneself, drive forward , (Xenophon Historicus):—;of sounds, to utter , (Aeschines Orator), etc. 10. to give up, let go: to give up to the enemy, (Thucydides), etc.; πρ. σφᾶς αὑτούς gave themselves up as lost , (Thucydides) 11. to desert, abandon , (Thucydides); οὐδαμῆ προί̈εντο ἑαυτούς did not lose themselves (i. e. take bribes), (Demosthenes Orator) 12. to give away, give freely , (Thucydides), etc.; προέσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων (Demosthenes Orator) 13. to throw off one's clothes, (Demosthenes Orator): and, in bad sense, to throw away , τὸν καιρόν (Demosthenes Orator); τὰ πατρῷα (Aeschines Orator): absolute to be lavish , (Aristotle Philosopher) 14. a second predicate is sometimes added, ἡμᾶς προέσθαι ἀδικουμένους to suffer us to be wronged, (Thucydides); προέμενοι αὐτοὺς ἀπολέσθαι (Xenophon Historicus); πρ. τινὶ ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατῆσαι (Demosthenes Orator) 15. to suffer to escape , (Polybius Historicus) 16. rarely in good sense, to give over to one, confide to one's care , (Xenophon Historicus) 17. to neglect, disregard , (Aristotle Philosopher):—; absolute to neglect all advice, to be reckless , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8897.d: 1. to set before; so in Mid., (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Pass., with aorist2 and perfect active, φυλακῆς μὴ προκαθεστηκυίας no guard having been set beforehand , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8898.d: 1. to seize beforehand, preoccupy , (Thucydides), etc.:—;Pass. to be preoccupied , (Thucydides) 2. metaphorically to anticipate, frustrate , (Thucydides):—;of persons, to anticipate or surprise them, (Thucydides) 3. to overpower before , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8902.d: to go out for foraging , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8903.d: 1. a foraging, a foraging expedition, foray , (Xenophon Historicus): in plural, foraging parties , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. an elephant's trunk , (Polybius Historicus) 3. = προ-νομία, (Lucian) (ML)

G8904.d: 1. an opening or introduction to a thing; in Music, a prelude, overture , (Pindar); in poems and speeches, a proem, preface, preamble, introduction , Lat. exordium, (Pindar) 2. metaphorically of any prelude or beginning , φροίμιον χορεύσομαι (Aeschulus Tragicus); μηδέπω ' ν προοιμίοις only just beginning , (Aeschulus Tragicus); εἴ τι τοῦδε φρ. ματᾷ if any part of this presage be vain, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. generally, a hymn , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8906.d: reckless haste, vehemence, rashness, indiscretion , (Demosthenes Orator), etc. from προπετής (ML)

G8907.d: 1. to fall or throw oneself forward , as in rowing, προπεσόντες ἔρεσσον, like Lat. incumbere remis, (Odyssey by Homer):—;of suppliants, to fall prostrate , (Euripides) 2. to rush forward, rush headlong , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to move forwards, advance before the rest, (Polybius Historicus): to project , (Polybius Historicus) 4. προπίτνω poetry for προπίπτω 5. to fall prostate , ἐς γᾶν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8908.d: in plural, like προπύλαια, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; in singular, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8909.d: a going up, ascent , κλίμακος προσαμβάσεις ascent by means of ladders, i. e. scaling ladders, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. (Euripides); τειχέων πρ. a place where they may be approached , (Euripides); δωμάτων πρ. i. e. the steps leading to the house, (Euripides) (ML)

G8911.d: 1. to strike or dash against , τί τινι (Iliad by Homer); ἀψῖδα πέτρῳ πρ. letting it dash against , (Euripides); τὸν πρὶν ὄλβον ἕρματι πρ. to wreck his happiness on a rock, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. θηρία τινί to set them on him, (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. δόρυ τινί (Euripides):—;without any notion of violence, to put to, apply , μαλακὰν χέρα πρ. [ ἕλκει] of a surgeon, (Pindar); πρ. παρειὰν παρηίδι (Euripides); ὄμματα τέκνοις (Euripides) 2. to assign to, procure for , κέρδος τινί (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. Λακεδαιμονίοις Ὀλυμπιάδα to give them the honour of an Olympic victory, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. κακὸν τῇ πόλει (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὔκλειαν σαυτῇ (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. δεῖμά τινι, Lat. incutere timorem alicui, (Euripides) 3. with accusative of the object struck, ἀρούρας προσβάλλειν, of the Sun, to strike the earth with his rays, (Homer); of smells, βροτοῦ [ ὀσμὴ] με προσέβαλε (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. metaphorically to attend to a thing or to add , (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. μή μ᾽ ἀνάγκῃ προσβάλῃς τάδ᾽ εἰκαθεῖν do not drive me by force to give way, (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. intransitive to strike against, to make an attack or assault upon , τινί (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; πρὸς τὸ τεῖχος (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to attack, charge , (Herdotus Historicus); προσβαλὼν αἱρεῖ τὴν πόλιν by assault , (Xenophon Historicus) 7. to put in with a ship, ἐς τὸν λιμένα (Thucydides); πρὸς Τάραντα (Thucydides); with dative, Σικελίᾳ (Thucydides) 8. Mid. to throw oneself upon, attack , τινα (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8916.d: to look at, behold , (Mimnermus Lyricus), etc.; compare aorist2 προσεῖδον:—;so in Mid., προσορωμένα (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8917.d: 1. to speak to one, to address, accost , (Homer), etc.; πρ. ὀνόματί τινα (Demosthenes Orator):—;with double accusative, τί προσείπω ς᾽ ἔπο; (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to address as so and so, πρ. τινὰ ὡς ἀλλότριον (Plato Philosophus); πρ. τινὰ χαίρειν to bid him greeting , (Euripides) 3. to call so and so, to name , τί νιν προσείπ; (Aeschulus Tragicus); τοῦτο γάρ ς᾽ ἔχω μόνον προσειπεῖν (Sophocles Tragicus); ὅν μοι προσεῖπας πόσιν whom thou didst name my husband, (Euripides) (ML)

G8920.d: over and above, besides , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8922.d: 1. soft, gentle, kindly , (Pindar); προσηνές τι λέγειν (Thucydides) 2. with dative, λύχνῳ προσηνές, i. e. suitable for burning, (Herdotus Historicus) (For derivation, see. ἀπηνής). 3. adverb -νῶς, (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8924.d: 1. a putting to, application of ladders to a wall, (Thucydides); of the cupping-glass, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. an adding, addition , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8926.d: to set on fire or burn besides :—;Pass., σκεύη προσκεκαυμένα pots burnt at the fire , (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically, προσκαίεσθαί τινι to be in love with . . , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8927.d: 1. to leave besides as a legacy , ἀρχήν τινι (Thucydides) 2. to lose besides , τὰ αὑτῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8929.d: 1. to be placed or laid by or upon, to lie by or upon , οὔατα προσέκειτο handles were upon it, (Iliad by Homer); τῇ θύρᾳ προσκεῖσθαι to keep close to the door, (Aristophanes Comicus); δοκοὶ τῷ τείχει προσκείμεναι lying near the wall, (Thucydides):—; ὁ προσκείμενος ἵππος the inside horse (turning a corner), (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to lie beside, cling to , (Sophocles Tragicus): of a woman, to be given to wife , τινί (Herdotus Historicus) 3. generally, to be involved in or bound up with good or evil, with dative, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to be attached or devoted to , τινί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πρ. τῷ λεγομένῳ to put faith in a story, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. οἴνῳ to be addicted to wine, (Herdotus Historicus); ἄγραις hunting, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 5. to press upon, be urgent with a person, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus); προσκείμενος with zeal , (Thucydides) 6. in military sense, to press close or hard, pursue closely , τινί (Thucydides); absolute to follow close , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ προσκείμενον the enemy , (Herdotus Historicus) 7. with a thing for the subject, to fall to, belong to , τοῖσι θεῶν τιμὴ αὕτη προσκέαται (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. τινι δοῦλος (Euripides):—; to be laid upon as a charge, to do something, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus) 8. to be added or attached to , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;absolute, ἡ χάρις προσκείσεται (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8931.d: 1. to strike against , τινί (Plato Philosophus):absolute to stumble, fail , (Plutarch) 2. to have a collision with another, give offence , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. τινί (Plutarch) 3. to take offence at, be angry with , τινί (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: —;absolute to take offence , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)
